name: Aran
overview: Aran was a male Edomite, identified specifically as the son of Dishan. His mention in Scripture is brief and focuses primarily on his lineage within the Edomite tribe. No additional personal details or notes are provided about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Aran is a proper name meaning 'wild goat.' This name is not indicated as given directly by God but is recorded in Genesis 36:28. The meaning reflects a common practice of Hebrew names relating to natural elements or animals.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Aran was the son of Dishan, establishing his direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Aran's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical records of the Edomites, descendants of Esau. His mention as the son of Dishan situates him within the broader narrative of Edomite lineage, which is important for understanding the tribal histories and relationships in the Old Testament. Although his role is not expanded upon, his presence in Genesis 36:28 confirms the historical and tribal identity of the Edomites as part of God's providential plan.
